catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extraction focused on non-agentic structural, domain, and infrastructure patterns from source code, configuration, and documentation.
analysis_limits: Source code limited to key files listed; not a full repo scan.
Evidence is inferred from file names and symbols; detailed file contents not fully examined.
Some patterns are inferred from naming conventions and project structure; validation recommended.

system_map.overview: The system is a Python-based runner and governance framework for an architecture-as-code environment. It consists of a CLI layer, a runner core, governance modules, LLM client adapters, and a knowledge repository. The system uses pydantic models for domain entities, a registry for governance actions, and a file-based knowledge store.

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: Core domain entities are modeled as Pydantic models, providing validation, serialization, and type safety.
patterns.intent: To represent domain concepts with robust data validation and clear contracts.
patterns.context: The system manages governance entities, capability records, and health metrics that require validation and structured representation.
forces: Need for type safety and validation across modules.
Desire for serialization to/from JSON/YAML for persistence.
Need to maintain consistency across different data sources.
patterns.solution: Use Pydantic models (e.g., GovernanceAction, CapabilityRecord, HealthStatus) to define schemas, validation rules, and serialization methods.
implementation_signals: Use of type hints and validators

evidence.note: Core governance entities as Pydantic models.
Domain entities for steering and capabilities.
Health status modeled as an enum and computed via function.

benefits: Data validation is centralized and consistent.
Models can be easily serialized for persistence or API responses.
costs: Overhead of Pydantic dependencies.
May need to update models when domain changes.
failure_modes: Models can become tightly coupled to persistence schemas.
Validation errors may be inconsistent if not handled globally.

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply to any new domain entity; consider using inheritance and composition to extend.

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: Governance transitions are managed through a registry of possible state changes, enabling controlled and traceable transitions.
patterns.intent: To model and enforce state transitions in governance processes, allowing new transitions to be added declaratively.
patterns.context: The GovernanceActionEngine uses a TransitionRegistry to define allowed transitions between states.
forces: Need to ensure governance objects only move through valid states.
Desire to make transition rules explicit and configurable.
Need to support traceability of state changes.
patterns.solution: Define a TransitionRegistry that maps source and target states to validation logic, and use a GovernanceActionEngine to orchestrate transitions.
implementation_signals: Methods for registering and validating transitions

evidence.note: Registry for state transitions and engine to execute them.

benefits: Easily extendable by adding new transitions to the registry.
costs: Can become complex if many states and transitions.
Requires careful design to avoid overlapping transitions.
failure_modes: Registry can become a god class if not structured.
Transition validation may be bypassed if not enforced centrally.

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply to any stateful governance process; keep transition definitions data-driven.

patterns.name: Strategy Pattern for LLM Clients
patterns.summary: Different LLM clients (real and mock) are used interchangeably through a common interface, enabling strategy selection.
patterns.intent: To isolate the system from LLM provider specifics and allow testing without external dependencies.
patterns.context: The system has a LiteLLMClient and a MockLLMClient in the llm module, suggesting a strategy pattern for LLM interaction.
forces: Need to switch between real LLM providers and mock implementations for testing.
Desire to keep LLM provider details out of core logic.
patterns.solution: Define a common interface for LLM clients, with concrete implementations for real and mock backends. Use dependency injection to select the appropriate client.
implementation_signals: Multiple classes implementing the same interface
Client used as an abstraction in other modules

benefits: Allows swapping providers without changing core logic.
costs: Requires a clear interface.
May add indirection.
failure_modes: Interface may not be comprehensive enough.
Clients may diverge in behavior.

patterns.reuse_notes: When adding new LLM providers, implement the common interface.

patterns.name: Health Calculation as Pure Function
patterns.summary: System health is computed by a pure function that takes inputs and returns a status and reasons.
patterns.intent: To keep health determination deterministic, testable, and independent of side effects.
patterns.context: The dashboard health_model.py contains calculate_health and get_health_reasons functions.
forces: Need for testability of health logic.
Desire to separate health computation from I/O.
patterns.solution: Implement calculate_health as a pure function with clear inputs and outputs, returning a HealthStatus enum and reasons.

costs: May become complex if many input parameters.
Requires explicit data passing.
failure_modes: If inputs are not well-defined, function may be misused.

patterns.reuse_notes: Use for any deterministic computation that should be pure.

patterns.name: Service Layer for Governance Actions
patterns.summary: Governance actions are orchestrated through a dedicated service layer, separating business logic from transport or UI.
patterns.intent: To centralize governance action handling and provide a clean API for the rest of the system.
patterns.context: A GovernanceActionService exists alongside the engine, suggesting a service layer that encapsulates use cases.
forces: Need for a consistent interface for triggering governance actions.
Desire to separate concerns between engine and service.
patterns.solution: Use a service class (GovernanceActionService) that wraps the engine and provides higher-level operations, e.g., `perform_action`.

evidence.note: Service layer for governance action execution.

benefits: Encapsulates business logic and transaction management.
Provides a clear API for callers.
costs: Adds an extra layer of abstraction.
May become a god service if too many responsibilities.
failure_modes: Service may become bloated.
May hide complex logic that belongs in domain.

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply when a subsystem requires a facade to orchestrate domain logic.

patterns.name: Composition over Inheritance for Governance Engines
patterns.summary: Governance engines are composed of smaller components (e.g., compliance engine, agentic merger) rather than using deep inheritance.
patterns.intent: To promote flexibility and reuse by combining independent modules.
patterns.context: The governance package contains separate engines for compliance, agentic merging, and action handling, which are likely composed together.
forces: Need for modular, testable components.
Desire to avoid rigid inheritance hierarchies.
patterns.solution: Design each engine as a standalone class with a specific responsibility, and have higher-level services compose them as needed.
implementation_signals: Multiple small classes with single responsibilities

evidence.note: Independent module for merging agentic outputs.

benefits: Each component is easier to test and maintain.
Flexibility to combine components in different ways.
costs: May require more boilerplate for assembly.
Interfaces must be well-defined.
failure_modes: Components may become coupled if not properly designed.
Complexity may shift to wiring logic.

patterns.reuse_notes: Favor composition when adding new governance capabilities.

patterns.name: Bootstrap Initialization Script
patterns.summary: A bootstrap module initializes the workspace by merging governance blocks and creating symlinks.
patterns.intent: To set up the environment and ensure consistent configuration across the repository.
patterns.context: src/cas_runner/bootstrap.py provides functions to merge governance blocks, merge Claude settings, and create symlinks.
forces: Need to ensure consistent configuration across different environments.
Desire to automate workspace setup.
patterns.solution: Provide a bootstrap function that performs initial setup steps, including file merging and symlink creation.

benefits: Simplifies setup for developers and CI.
costs: May be complex and non-deterministic if not idempotent.
File operations can have side effects.
failure_modes: Symlink creation may fail on some platforms.
Merges may overwrite user changes if not careful.

patterns.reuse_notes: Ensure idempotency and test on multiple operating systems.

patterns.name: Repository Pattern for Knowledge
patterns.summary: Knowledge artifacts are stored in a structured directory tree, serving as a repository for decisions, models, and patterns.
patterns.intent: To provide a consistent and searchable storage for knowledge artifacts.
patterns.context: The cas-knowledge/ directory contains templates, global, projects, and runtime subdirectories, suggesting a repository pattern.
forces: Need for persistent storage of knowledge artifacts.
Desire to organize by type and scope.
patterns.solution: Define a directory structure with clear categories (global, projects, runtime) and template files for consistency.

costs: Manual organization can drift without tooling.
May require a governance layer to manage.
failure_modes: Directory structure may become inconsistent.
Templates may be bypassed.

patterns.reuse_notes: Use as a reference for organizing knowledge repositories.

patterns.name: Configuration Merging Heuristic
patterns.summary: Instead of overwriting configuration files, the system merges new governance blocks and settings into existing files.
patterns.intent: To preserve user-customized settings while providing updates.
patterns.context: The bootstrap module merges governance blocks and Claude settings into existing configuration files.
forces: Need to update settings without losing user customizations.
Desire to automate configuration management.
patterns.solution: Implement merge functions that combine existing content with new content, with conflict resolution rules.
implementation_signals: Use of YAML or JSON parsing and merging

costs: Merge logic can be complex and error-prone.
Need to handle edge cases like conflicting keys.
failure_modes: Merging may produce unexpected results if not tested.
May introduce security concerns if merging untrusted content.

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply to any file-based configuration management.

patterns.name: Template-Driven Artifact Consistency
patterns.summary: Knowledge artifacts are created from predefined templates, ensuring consistency across the repository.
patterns.intent: To standardize the structure of architecture documents, ADRs, and pattern entries.
patterns.context: The cas-knowledge/templates directory contains multiple markdown templates for various artifacts.
forces: Need to maintain consistent documentation.
Desire to lower the barrier for contributing knowledge.
patterns.solution: Provide a set of markdown templates that users copy and fill in, with sections defined by the system.

costs: Templates may be too rigid for some use cases.
Users may not follow templates exactly.
failure_modes: Templates may become outdated.
Inconsistency if templates are not enforced by tooling.

patterns.reuse_notes: Regularly review and update templates based on actual needs.

patterns.name: Separation of Pure and Effectful Functions
patterns.summary: The codebase distinguishes between pure functions (e.g., health calculation) and effectful operations (e.g., file I/O, LLM calls).
patterns.intent: To improve testability and reasoning about the system.
patterns.context: Health calculation is pure, while bootstrap and LLM clients have side effects.
forces: Need to easily test business logic.
Desire to isolate side effects for maintenance.
patterns.solution: Keep pure logic in separate modules (e.g., health_model.py) and effectful operations in dedicated infrastructure modules.
implementation_signals: Clear interfaces between pure and effectful parts

benefits: Pure functions are easy to test and reuse.
Side effects are localized, simplifying maintenance.
costs: May require additional layers of abstraction.
failure_modes: Pure functions can accidentally perform I/O if not careful.
Boundaries may blur over time.

patterns.reuse_notes: Enforce this separation by coding standards and code reviews.

patterns.name: Adapter Pattern for External Dependencies
patterns.summary: External dependencies like LLM providers are wrapped behind interfaces, allowing for interchangeable implementations.
patterns.intent: To shield the core from vendor-specific APIs and enable cross-provider compatibility.
patterns.context: The LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient provide two implementations for LLM interaction.
forces: Need to switch between providers and mock.
Desire to avoid vendor lock-in.
patterns.solution: Define a common interface for LLM clients, with concrete classes that adapt to the specific provider (LiteLLM, mock).
implementation_signals: Multiple classes with the same method signatures
Use of an abstract base class or protocol

benefits: Core is independent of LLM vendor.
Testing is simplified with mock client.
costs: Extra layers of abstraction.
failure_modes: Interface may not cover all provider features.
Adapters may drift from the core interface.

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply to any external service integration.

patterns.name: Module-Based Layering for Clean Architecture
patterns.summary: The codebase is structured into modules with clear responsibilities: governance, steering, dashboard, llm, and core.
patterns.intent: To achieve separation of concerns and maintainability.
patterns.context: The src/cas_runner directory contains submodules: governance/, steering/, dashboard/, llm/.
forces: Need to manage complexity of an evolving system.
Desire to isolate changes to specific areas.
patterns.solution: Organize code into modules that mirror architectural layers: application logic (runner), domain models, and infrastructure adapters.
implementation_signals: Dependency direction from higher to lower modules

evidence.note: Domain and application logic for governance.

benefits: Easier to test modules in isolation.
costs: Requires discipline to maintain dependency direction.
May lead to over-abstraction.
failure_modes: Circular dependencies if not managed.
Modules can become too large.

patterns.reuse_notes: Follow when adding new features: place domain logic in domain module, infrastructure in infrastructure.

patterns.name: CI Replace Hardcoded Workflows
patterns.summary: CI/CD workflows are validated to avoid hardcoded values and unreachable steps, using a validation script.
patterns.intent: To maintain robust and maintainable CI/CD pipelines.
patterns.context: The spec '090-simplify-cicd-workflows' includes a validation script that checks for hardcoding, unpinned installers, unreachable dry runs, and retired workflows.
forces: Need to keep CI/CD pipelines reliable.
Desire to enforce best practices across workflows.
patterns.solution: Create a Python validation script that inspects workflow YAML files and reports violations.

costs: Need to keep validation rules up to date.
May produce false positives.
failure_modes: Validation script may not cover all cases.
Workflow changes may bypass checks.

patterns.reuse_notes: Extend the script as new workflow patterns emerge.

anti_patterns.name: Potential God Object: Governance Action Engine
symptoms: GovernanceActionEngine might handle multiple responsibilities: transition registration, state mutation, and rule enforcement.
High number of methods and dependencies.
impact: Changes in one responsibility may break others.
suggested_remediation: Decompose engine into smaller classes: TransitionManager, Validator, Executor.

anti_patterns.name: Unclear Dependency Direction Between Modules
symptoms: High-level modules (e.g., runner) may directly depend on low-level infrastructure (e.g., llm clients), bypassing abstractions.
suggested_remediation: Define and enforce dependency rules using architecture tests (e.g., import-linter).

anti_patterns.name: Missing Separation Between Domain and Persistence Models
symptoms: Pydantic models are used for both domain logic and persistence, leading to potential coupling.
No clear repository interface for storage.
impact: Changes in storage format affect domain logic.
Harder to test domain without infrastructure.
suggested_remediation: Define repository interfaces and separate persistence models from domain models.

anti_patterns.name: Hardcoded Paths and Configuration
symptoms: Potential hardcoded file paths in bootstrap or other modules.
Configuration may be scattered across files.
suggested_remediation: Use configuration files and environment variables.

anti_patterns.name: Potential Redundant Validation Scripts
symptoms: Multiple validation scripts or checks may overlap (e.g., validate_workflows.py vs other quality gates).
Duplicated logic for YAML parsing and rule checking.
suggested_remediation: Centralize validation logic into a shared module.
Use a single linting/validation entry point.

cross_cutting_concerns.description: The system manages configuration through merging and templates, but lacks a unified configuration service.
Pydantic models provide validation, but there is no global error handling strategy observed.
OpenTelemetry dependencies suggested, but no explicit logging patterns emerged in the analysed files.
The system uses registries and strategy patterns to enable extension, but lacks a plugin mechanism.
Pure functions and mock clients facilitate testing, but no unit test files were observed.
